# Copilot Prompt Library

Last updated: 2026-10-17 · Owner: BSA Manager

- **Purpose:** the team's tested prompts for Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, each paired with the check that must follow it. A prompt without its Verify step is not a library entry. The rules behind every entry (what you may paste, the sandbox rule, maker-checker) are in `docs/primers/copilot-chat-guide.md`.
- **Who uses it:** everyone on the team. Hire A and Hire B propose entries; the Manager reviews them. The live copy is a page in the team OneNote section ([COMPANY: team OneNote section for the prompt library]); this file is its template and starter set.
- **When:** from W1, when the starter entries are introduced in the M11 setup and rules session. Each hire aims to propose a first entry by the day-60 review and has 3 entries reviewed by the Manager by the day-90 review (a day-90 Should criterion, `docs/01-30-60-90-plan.md` Section 4). Only entries the hire added count; the starter set does not. The Manager re-checks the library at each milestone review and retires stale entries. Module M11.

## How to use an entry

1. Open a new Copilot Chat, signed in with your work account (enterprise data protection shield visible; guide 1.4).
2. Copy the prompt. Replace each `[PASTE: ...]` with material you paste or upload, and each `[FILL: ...]` with a short value you type. Follow the paste rules in guide 2.2: no credentials, no personal data, company data only with the Manager's agreement.
3. Run it, then iterate (guide 3.5).
4. Do the Verify step every time, even when the output looks right.
5. Log the use in your Copilot use log with the entry ID (guide 6.1).

## How to add an entry and get it reviewed

1. **Prove it first.** Use the prompt at least twice in real work with a verified result, both in your use log.
2. **Make it generic.** Placeholders for all material. No company, tool, system object, person, supplier, customer, broker or item names, and no data.
3. **Write the Verify step.** Name the primary source or control and a check someone else could repeat, for example "tick every row against the notice; the annex count equals the table count". "Check the output" is not a Verify step.
4. **Add it.** Add a row at the end of the table with the next free ID, "Added by" your initials and date, and status Proposed. Tell the Manager in Teams or at the 1:1.
5. **Review.** The Manager reviews it against the quality checklist below (about 5 minutes, in work review time), then adds initials and date and sets the status to Reviewed, or writes what to change in the change log.
6. **Fix it when a use shows a gap.** Edit the entry, set the status back to Proposed, and record the change in the change log.
7. **Retire, don't delete.** When an entry stops working (a product change, a new template), set the status to Retired.

If [COMPANY: confirm sharing prompts to a team is allowed], also save Reviewed entries in the Copilot Prompt Gallery and share them with the team in Teams. This page stays the master, because the Verify step lives here.

### Status values

| Status | Meaning |
|---|------------------|
| Starter | Written with this template. The Manager reviews the starter set before the W1 session; test an entry once with fictional data before its first real use |
| Proposed | Added by a team member; not yet reviewed |
| Reviewed | The Manager checked it against the quality checklist |
| Retired | No longer used; kept for the record |

## Quality checklist for an entry (used in the Manager's review)

- [ ] Generic: placeholders for all material; no company, tool, system object, person, supplier, customer, broker or item names; no data.
- [ ] Safe: following it cannot lead anyone to paste credentials, personal data or restricted data, or to run code on production.
- [ ] Follows the guide's pattern: goal, context, a pasted or uploaded source, expectations; asks for assumptions, or for MISSING or OPEN QUESTION markers, wherever Copilot could invent facts.
- [ ] The Verify step names the source or control and a concrete check another person could repeat.
- [ ] Respects the boundary rule and maker-checker: no scope decisions in a Standard Cost prompt, no $ in a Research prompt, no output sent unreviewed.
- [ ] Used at least twice with a verified result (the use log entries are named in the change log).
